papers.title: Melatonin-loaded proniosomes enhance gemcitabine response in gemcitabine-resistant cholangiocarcinoma: Proteomic and computational insights.
papers.abstract: Acquired resistance to gemcitabine (GEM) remains a major barrier in cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) therapy. Melatonin has multi-targeted antitumor activity but is limited by rapid elimination and low oral bioavailability. We developed a maltodextrin-based melatonin-loaded proniosome (MPN) and evaluated its physicochemical properties, ex vivo permeation, and antitumor activity, alone and with GEM, in a GEM-resistant CCA model. MPN was prepared by a provesicular slurry method and characterized for physicochemical properties, stability, molecular dynamics (MD), and ex vivo permeation. Efficacy and tole
papers.summary: This study developed a maltodextrin-based melatonin-loaded proniosome (MPN) formulation to overcome melatonin's poor bioavailability and tested it, alone and combined with gemcitabine, in a gemcitabine-resistant cholangiocarcinoma model. MPN improved physicochemical stability and permeation, and the combination enhanced antitumor efficacy against resistant cells. Proteomic and computational analyses were used to explore the mechanisms underlying the reversal of gemcitabine resistance.

papers.title: Exploring the role and mechanism of methionine metabolism in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps based on bioinformatics analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps (CRSwNP) affects 1%-4% of the global population with high recurrence rates. While methionine metabolism abnormalities contribute to various inflammatory diseases, their role in CRSwNP pathogenesis remains unclear. This study aimed to systematically investigate the role of methionine metabolism in CRSwNP and identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets through integrating multi-omics data and interpretable machine learning approaches.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with interpretable machine learning to investigate how methionine metabolism contributes to chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP). The authors identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets linked to methionine metabolic pathways, suggesting a role for this metabolism in disease pathogenesis. The work is exploratory and based on bioinformatics analysis, so experimental validation would be needed to confirm the findings.

papers.title: DBAASP V4: condition-resolved bioactivity and chemical structures for data-driven peptide and peptidomimetic discovery.
papers.abstract: The current peptide renaissance-driven by metagenomic and proteomic mining, molecular de-extinction, protein language models, and generative or evolutionary design-is producing millions of candidates, but useful machine learning depends on experimentally anchored, context-rich labels. The Database of Antimicrobial Activity and Structure of Peptides (DBAASP) is a manually curated resource linking peptides and peptidomimetics to quantitative antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anticancer, hemolytic, and mammalian-cell cytotoxicity measurements and their experimental conditions. DBAASP v4 contains >25 00
papers.summary: DBAASP v4 is a manually curated database linking peptides and peptidomimetics to quantitative bioactivity measurements (antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anticancer, hemolytic, cytotoxicity) along with the experimental conditions under which they were obtained. The update adds chemical structures and condition-resolved data, providing context-rich labels needed to train machine learning models for peptide and peptidomimetic discovery.

papers.title: Identifying phase separation modulators mediated by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein using a structure-based drug discovery approach.
papers.abstract: As severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to evolve through mutations and acquire resistance to existing antiviral agents, the persistence of post-pandemic infections remains a significant global health concern. To address these challenges, it is crucial to develop novel therapeutic agents that target previously unexplored viral or host mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study uses a structure-based drug discovery approach to identify small molecules that modulate phase separation driven by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein, a mechanism not targeted by existing antivirals. The work aims to uncover new therapeutic candidates that could remain effective despite viral mutation and resistance.

papers.title: PROTAC-DB 4.0: an expanded knowledgebase of targeted protein degradation modalities with AI-powered knowledge discovery.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) represent an emerging therapeutic modality that harnesses the ubiquitin-proteasome system to induce targeted protein degradation (TPD). Their event-driven and catalytic mechanisms provide new opportunities to target previously undruggable proteins. However, the rapid expansion of TPD technologies, including molecular glues (MGs) and X-functional targeting chimeras (XTACs), together with the increasing application of artificial intelligence (AI) in degrader design, highlights the need for comprehensive and continuously updated data resources. Here, we pr
papers.summary: PROTAC-DB 4.0 is an updated knowledgebase that now covers a broader range of targeted protein degradation modalities, including PROTACs, molecular glues, and XTACs, alongside AI-driven design data. It adds AI-powered knowledge discovery features to help researchers navigate the rapidly growing TPD literature and compound data. The resource aims to support degrader design and target identification for previously undruggable proteins.

papers.title: Unlocking the electronic and adsorption origin of doping-engineered WS2 monolayers: a DFT investigation with machine learning validation.
papers.abstract: Defect-engineered tungsten disulfide (WS2) monolayers provide a tunable platform for clarifying how local dopant chemistry that converts weak gas adsorption into measurable electronic perturbation. Here, N-doped and N-O co-doped WS2 monolayers are investigated to decouple adsorption strength from electronic-response descriptors toward CO, CO2, and NH3 sensing. Machine learning force field (MLFF)-assisted DFT calculations show that MLFF reproduces the DFT energy-force relationships and phonon trends for pristine WS2 and N-WS2, whereas the larger deviations for N-O-WS2 indicate that co-doped con
papers.summary: This study uses DFT calculations, validated by a machine learning force field, to examine how nitrogen doping and nitrogen-oxygen co-doping of WS2 monolayers change their electronic response and adsorption behavior toward CO, CO2, and NH3. The authors show that dopant chemistry can decouple adsorption strength from electronic-response descriptors, providing design principles for gas sensing. The MLFF reproduces DFT energy-force and phonon trends well for pristine and N-doped WS2 but deviates more for the co-doped system.

papers.title: General prediction of T cell receptor antigen specificity from sequence using AlphaFold 3.
papers.abstract: The major histocompatibility complex (MHC):peptide:T cell receptor (TCR) complex is the most diverse trimolecular interface known in nature and a key trigger for adaptive immunity. TCRs are now routinely sequenced at scale; however, decoding their specificity for antigens remains a bottleneck. While in silico approaches have advanced considerably, none enables prediction against "unseen" epitopes, limiting their applicability to a tiny fraction of cases. Here, we show that AlphaFold 3 (AF3) predicts the structures of MHC:peptide:TCR triads with unprecedented accuracy. By applying AF3 to >9000
papers.summary: The authors demonstrate that AlphaFold 3 can predict MHC:peptide:TCR tri molecular structures with unprecedented accuracy, and they leverage this to build a model that predicts TCR antigen specificity even for epitopes not seen during training. By applying AF3 to over 9,000 complexes, they show structure-based prediction can generalize to unseen antigens, addressing a major bottleneck in decoding TCR specificity from sequence.

papers.title: Aspergillus terreus MAK153 against Fusarium oxysporum: biocontrol, metabolites, and simvastatin docking.
papers.abstract: This study demonstrates the considerable antagonistic activity of Aspergillus terreus MAK153 against a pathogenic Fusarium oxysporum AUMC3191 isolate. In dual culture assay, soil-isolated Aspergillus terreus Thom effectively hindered F. oxysporum AUMC3191 growth and impressively blocked zearalenone (ZEN) synthesis. Scanning electron microscopy demonstrated significant damage to F. oxysporum hyphae, such as abnormalities, shrinkage, bending, and deformity. Molecular identification through rDNA ITS sequence analysis confirmed the isolate as Aspergillus terreus, registered in GeneBank (Accession
papers.summary: The soil-derived fungus Aspergillus terreus MAK153 strongly inhibits growth of the plant pathogen Fusarium oxysporum in dual-culture assays, blocking production of the mycotoxin zearalenone and visibly damaging Fusarium hyphae. The authors identify the isolate by ITS sequencing and use metabolite profiling plus molecular docking of simvastatin to explore the antifungal basis of the interaction.

papers.title: ARIEL: an openly accessible database of experimental RNA-ligand binding affinities paired with 3D structures.
papers.abstract: RNA is an increasingly attractive target for small-molecule therapeutics, yet the rational design and computational modelling of RNA-binding small molecules are constrained by the scarcity of experimentally measured binding affinities linked to 3D structures. Here we present ARIEL (Affinity Resource for Interactions of RNA and Ligands), an openly accessible, manually curated database that pairs experimentally determined dissociation constants (Kd) of RNA-ligand complexes with the corresponding experimental structures. We screened 6954 RNA-containing structures from the Protein Data Bank, extra
papers.summary: ARIEL is a new, openly accessible database that manually curates experimentally measured RNA-ligand binding affinities (Kd values) and pairs them with corresponding 3D structures from the Protein Data Bank. By screening 6,954 RNA-containing structures, the resource addresses a key bottleneck in RNA-targeted drug discovery: the lack of affinity data linked to structural information. This enables better computational modeling and rational design of small molecules that bind RNA.

papers.title: Harnessing engineered laccase and functional carrier materials for efficient dye degradation: From mechanism to application.
papers.abstract: Laccases are copper-containing oxidases that have been widely investigated for the decolorization and degradation of synthetic dyes, including azo, anthraquinone, triphenylmethane, indigo and thiazine dyes. However, their application in dye-containing wastewater remains constrained by enzyme instability under complex effluent conditions, limited oxidation of some recalcitrant or high-redox-potential dyes, mediator dependence, and poor recovery and reuse of free laccase. This review discusses recent progress in laccase-catalyzed dye degradation from a mechanism-to-engineering perspective, linki
papers.summary: This review examines recent advances in using laccase enzymes, combined with engineered carrier materials, to degrade synthetic dyes in wastewater. It connects the underlying catalytic mechanisms to practical engineering solutions that address enzyme instability, limited oxidation of recalcitrant dyes, mediator dependence, and poor enzyme recovery and reuse.

papers.title: Wrapping mechanism of β-lactoglobulin around SDS micelles characterized by time-resolved vacuum-ultraviolet circular dichroism and molecular dynamics simulation.
papers.abstract: Conformational transitions of water-soluble proteins at membrane interfaces play an important role in biological functions and diseases. Herein, we present a novel analytical framework capable of revealing the unique stepwise wrapping of β-lactoglobulin (bLG) around anionic sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) micelles by integrating time-resolved vacuum-ultraviolet circular dichroism (TR-VUVCD) spectroscopy with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. TR-VUVCD spectra of bLG interacting with SDS micelles were measured over 0.4-90 s, revealing that this interaction induces a β-to-α conformational transit
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.summary: This study combines time-resolved vacuum-ultraviolet circular dichroism spectroscopy with molecular dynamics simulations to characterize how β-lactoglobulin wraps around anionic SDS micelles. The authors observe a stepwise, β-to-α conformational transition occurring over 0.4–90 seconds, revealing a novel wrapping mechanism at membrane interfaces. The work provides a new analytical framework for studying protein conformational dynamics at lipid-like surfaces.

papers.title: Simulating Directed Evolution In Silico with an Iterative, Physics-Based Workflow.
papers.abstract: Directed evolution consistently delivers engineered enzymes that facilitate diverse biocatalytic transformations. Despite advances in automation and high-throughput workflows, our ability to rapidly engineer novel enzymes is limited by our inability to thoroughly sample the vast protein design space. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) methods have alleviated this challenge to some degree, due to their ability to propose mutations based on learned patterns from complex protein data sets. However, the hidden logic of these AI-based methods can complicate our ability to reveal and exploit fu
papers.summary: This paper presents an iterative, physics-based computational workflow that mimics directed evolution in silico to engineer enzymes. Unlike generative AI methods whose decision-making is opaque, this approach uses physics-based scoring to propose and evaluate mutations across cycles, aiming to make the design process more interpretable and controllable. The work addresses the challenge of efficiently sampling the vast protein sequence space for enzyme engineering.

papers.title: Discovery and Design of YTHDF2-Selective and Pan-YTHDF Inhibitors for m6A Binding by the YTH Aromatic Cage.
papers.abstract: Recognition of N6-methyl-adenosine (m6A) in the RNA sequences by the YT521-B homology domain-containing protein family paralogs 1-3 (YTHDF1-3) is a dominant layer of myriad cellular regulation. Dysregulated YTHDF paralog expression and activities have been reported in cancer, including glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) in which YTHDF2 has been identified as a druggable dependency. Guided by structure-based in silico screening, we identified structurally related small-molecule compound families of promising YTHDF inhibitor compounds. Following in vitro screening, two hits, DT11 and DT15, emerged an
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening to identify small-molecule inhibitors that bind the m6A-recognition aromatic cage of YTHDF proteins, yielding compounds DT11 and DT15 with selectivity for YTHDF2 as well as pan-YTHDF activity. This provides early chemical probes for targeting m6A reader function, with potential relevance to YTHDF2-dependent cancers such as glioblastoma.

papers.title: Substrate recognition and stage-dependent transformation of aflatoxin B1 by mediator-free Bacillus laccase frL103.
papers.abstract: Enzyme-based mitigation of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is commonly evaluated by parent-toxin depletion. This study characterized the stage-dependent, mediator-free transformation of AFB1 by recombinant Bacillus laccase frL103 and assessed chemical, biological, and structural outcomes. UHPLC-HRMS profiling at 0, 30, and 60 h yielded 2846 filtered features and showed that the AFB1 response decreased to 23.8% and 14.8% of the initial value at 30 and 60 h, respectively. A feature at m/z 329.0660 increased at 30 h and declined to 17.7% of that response at 60 h; accurate mass and MS/MS fragmentation support
papers.summary: This study characterizes how a recombinant Bacillus laccase (frL103) degrades aflatoxin B1 without requiring a mediator, tracking the reaction over 60 hours. Using UHPLC-HRMS profiling, the authors show that AFB1 levels drop to ~24% and ~15% of initial at 30 and 60 hours, while a transient intermediate at m/z 329.0660 appears at 30 hours and then declines, indicating stage-dependent transformation rather than simple depletion. The work highlights that parent-toxin loss alone is an incomplete measure of detoxification and provides structural evidence for intermediate products.

papers.title: Bisphenol A induces ACSL4-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury: Implications for Hunner-type interstitial cystitis.
papers.abstract: Hunner-type interstitial cystitis (HIC) is an inflammatory subtype of interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome marked by persistent urothelial injury and bladder dysfunction. Bisphenol A (BPA) can disturb redox and inflammatory homeostasis, but its relevance to HIC-associated urothelial vulnerability remains unclear. This study examined whether acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) contributes to BPA-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury. Among non-pregnant adult women, higher creatinine-corrected urinary BPA was associated with a phenotype predominantly characteriz
papers.summary: This study links bisphenol A (BPA) exposure to urothelial injury resembling ferroptosis and cellular aging, mediated in part by ACSL4, in the context of Hunner-type interstitial cystitis. In a human cohort, higher urinary BPA correlated with a related phenotype, and mechanistic experiments support an ACSL4-associated ferro-aging pathway. The work suggests BPA may contribute to bladder urothelial vulnerability in this inflammatory bladder pain syndrome.

papers.title: On the limits of marginal protein folding stability: methodological goals and drawbacks.
papers.abstract: Why do proteins remain at the edge of stability rather than evolving toward maximal thermodynamic robustness? Can we trust the computational methods that inform about when and how stability falls off that edge? Marginal stability, the confinement of protein folding free energies to a window of approximately 5-15 kcal/mol, is broadly observed in biophysics, and its mechanistic causes, involving evolutionary and biophysical properties, remain under debate and require accurate predictions. In this regard, protein folding stability is currently predicted using both traditional structure-based homo
papers.summary: This paper examines why proteins evolve to be only marginally stable rather than maximally stable, a widely observed phenomenon where folding free energies cluster in a narrow 5-15 kcal/mol window. It critically evaluates the computational methods used to predict protein folding stability and discusses their methodological goals and limitations, questioning whether current predictions are reliable enough to explain the mechanistic causes of marginal stability.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Relative Ligand Binding Free Energy Simulation Methods: Amber-TI, GROMACS-NETI, OpenMM-FEP, and BLaDE-MSLD.
papers.abstract: Structure-based drug design has become increasingly important in the pharmaceutical industry for accelerating the discovery of effective drug candidates. In particular, ligand binding free energy serves as a critical metric for predicting drug efficacy during the key stages of hit discovery and lead optimization. Continuous progress has been made in the prediction of ligand binding free energies, but direct comparisons of different methods using the same force field remain challenging due to their unique implementations in different simulation engines. In this study, we present a direct compar
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: This study directly compares four relative ligand binding free energy simulation methods (Amber-TI, GROMACS-NETI, OpenMM-FEP, and BLaDE-MSLD) using the same force field, overcoming the usual obstacle of differing implementations across simulation engines. The comparison provides a benchmark of accuracy and performance across these widely used alchemical free energy approaches for structure-based drug design. It offers practical guidance for choosing a method for hit discovery and lead optimization.

papers.title: SynBioFooDB: a comprehensive resource for synthetic biology-driven food biomanufacturing.
papers.abstract: Enabled by synthetic biology and metabolic engineering, microbial biomanufacturing is reshaping the production of food-related compounds by offering sustainable alternatives to resource-intensive extraction and conventional chemical synthesis. However, information linking food-related compounds to biosynthetic pathways and microbial biomanufacturing evidence remains fragmented across the literature and poorly represented in existing food-oriented resources, hindering cross-study comparison, evidence synthesis, and rational design of microbial production systems. Here, we present SynBioFooDB (h
papers.summary: SynBioFooDB is a new database that consolidates information on food-related compounds, their biosynthetic pathways, and evidence for microbial biomanufacturing. It addresses the fragmentation of this knowledge across literature and existing food resources, enabling cross-study comparison and rational design of microbial production systems for food compounds.

papers.title: DockBind: A Quality-Controlled Data Set of Modeled Protein-Ligand Complexes Associated with Affinity Data.
papers.abstract: Ligand-protein interaction prediction is essential for structure-based drug discovery, but further development of machine-learning scoring functions is limited by a lack of high-quality training data sets. Here, we present DockBind, a curated data set of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, generated through a quality-controlled docking workflow. This workflow was developed based on an expanded docking benchmark, where we systematically evaluated free and template-based docking methods as well as ligand similarity and maximum common substructure (MCS
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: DockBind is a curated dataset of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, built through a quality-controlled docking workflow. The authors developed the workflow using an expanded docking benchmark that systematically evaluated free and template-based docking methods along with ligand similarity and maximum common substructure approaches. This resource aims to address the shortage of high-quality training data for machine-learning scoring functions in structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: A piperamide natural compound is compatible with an inactive DFG-out conformation of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2: In silico and in vitro model study.
papers.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR2) is a well-known key regulator of angiogenic cancers. In a structure-based virtual screening of Indonesian natural compounds, dehydropipernonaline (DPN), a piperamide from Piper species, emerged as a promising VEGFR2-binding candidate. However, its inhibitory activity against VEGFR2 has not been experimentally validated. This study combined molecular simulations and cellular assays to investigate the potential interaction between DPN and VEGFR2. Molecular docking predicted that DPN occupies the regulatory domain pocket (RDP) spanning the ca
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening to identify dehydropipernonaline (DPN), a piperamide natural compound from Piper species, as a candidate VEGFR2 binder that appears to occupy the regulatory domain pocket and stabilize an inactive DFG-out conformation. The authors combined molecular docking/simulation with cellular assays to validate the predicted interaction, supporting DPN as a potential anti-angiogenic agent. The work bridges computational screening of natural products with experimental validation for cancer-related kinase targeting.

papers.title: Small genomes, big lessons: What viruses teach us about structure-based riboregulation.
papers.abstract: RNA viruses encode multiple layers of information within a single molecule, which functions simultaneously as a template for protein synthesis and as a structured regulatory RNA. These structures control key aspects of viral gene expression, govern host interactions, and mediate immune evasion. Although the prevalence of RNA structure in viral genomes is now well established, only recently have functional and mechanistic studies begun to uncover how these elements act as regulatory modules that shape infection outcomes. With their compact genomes and experimentally tractable life cycles, RNA v
papers.summary: This review discusses how RNA viruses pack regulatory information into structured RNA elements within their compact genomes, using the same RNA molecule both as a protein-coding template and as a structured regulatory module. It highlights recent functional and mechanistic studies showing how these RNA structures control viral gene expression, host interactions, and immune evasion, and argues that viruses are powerful models for understanding structure-based riboregulation more broadly.

papers.title: Mapping Functional Transitions across Protein Homologues from a Single Simulation: Application of gEDES-HM to Adenylate Kinases.
papers.abstract: Proteins fluctuate across different conformational states, which constitute a dynamic ensemble that regulates their interaction networks and functions. Predicting the conformational landscape remains a computational challenge, and even more difficult is capturing the link between state distributions and specific functions within protein homologues. Here, we present gEDES-HM (generalized Ensemble Docking with Enhanced sampling of pocket Shape-Homology Modeling), a scalable computational protocol enabling us to remap conformational ensembles obtained from enhanced sampling simulations of a singl
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors introduce gEDES-HM, a computational protocol that uses enhanced sampling simulations of a single protein to map conformational ensembles onto homologous proteins, thereby predicting functional transitions across the family. Applied to adenylate kinases, the method captures how differences in conformational state distributions relate to functional variation among homologues. This offers a scalable way to study protein dynamics and function without running expensive simulations for every homologue.

papers.title: Physical determinants of reliable RNA-ligand binding prediction revealed by P-RISE.
papers.abstract: RNA-targeted small-molecule discovery is challenged by the scarcity of experimentally characterized RNA-ligand complexes and by the limited transferability of current computational approaches across chemically diverse systems. Here we present P-RISE, a physics-grounded framework for RNA-ligand binding prediction, and use it to identify the physical determinants underlying reliable performance. Systematic evaluation of force fields, ionic environments, dielectric treatments, and entropy corrections reveals three coupled requirements: preservation of RNA-binding pocket integrity under ion-sensit
papers.summary: The authors introduce P-RISE, a physics-based framework for predicting RNA-small molecule binding, and use systematic testing to identify what makes such predictions reliable. They find that accurate results require preserving the RNA binding pocket's structural integrity under different ionic conditions, along with careful treatment of force fields, dielectric effects, and entropy. This work clarifies the physical requirements for trustworthy RNA-ligand binding prediction, a key step for RNA-targeted drug discovery.

papers.title: In-silico transcriptomic characterization analysis identifies SMAD5, USP2, and CUL4A as key biomarkers and therapeutic targets in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a molecularly heterogeneous malignancy requiring reproducible biomarkers and structurally tractable therapeutic targets. We applied an integrated transcriptomic, network, virtual-screening, docking, ADMET, and molecular-dynamics (MD) workflow using GSE8671, GSE14333, and GSE89076. Differential expression analysis (adjusted p < 0.05, |log2FC= ≥ 1) identified 2092 upregulated/9130 downregulated genes in GSE8671, 926/945 in GSE14333, and 2317/1456 in GSE89076. Cross-dataset concordance was highest between GSE8671 and GSE89076 (r = 0.70), with 1040 shared upregulated and
papers.summary: The authors integrated transcriptomic data from three colorectal cancer datasets with network analysis, virtual screening, docking, ADMET, and molecular dynamics to identify SMAD5, USP2, and CUL4A as candidate biomarkers and druggable targets. Cross-dataset concordance was modest (r=0.70 between the two most similar datasets), and the work is entirely computational with no experimental validation.

papers.title: A multi-omics computational framework identifies cell-type-specific therapeutic targets and active compounds of Tripterygium wilfordii Hook.f. against diabetic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of chronic and end-stage kidney disease, and current therapies leave patients at high risk. Tripterygium wilfordii Hook.f. (TWHF), a traditional Chinese medicine, reduces proteinuria in DKD, but the compounds and molecular targets responsible remain poorly defined. We hypothesized that specific bioactive compounds of TWHF ameliorate DKD through interactions with cell-type-specific molecular targets, thereby modulating inflammatory, immune, and tissue-remodeling pathways involved in disease progression. By integrating transcriptomic analysis, imm
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic and other multi-omics data to identify cell-type-specific molecular targets of the traditional Chinese medicine Tripterygium wilfordii Hook.f. (TWHF) in diabetic kidney disease. The authors link specific bioactive compounds from TWHF to these targets and show they modulate inflammatory, immune, and tissue-remodeling pathways. The work provides a computational framework for repurposing herbal medicine compounds with cell-type resolution.

papers.title: Structure-guided development of G protein-biased apelin receptor agonists for cardiovascular disease.
papers.abstract: Apelin receptor (APLNR) is a crucial G protein-coupled receptor that plays a central role in cardiovascular homeostasis; therefore, it represents a promising therapeutic target for heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiac hypertrophy, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. However, the activation of APLNR simultaneously engages inhibitory G protein (Gi)-mediated protective signaling and β-arrestin pathways that are associated with pathological cardiac remodeling, thereby imposing significant limitations and challenges for the therapeutic development of conventional balanced agonists. Recent
papers.journal: Journal of Zhejiang University. Science. B
papers.summary: This paper describes the structure-guided design of apelin receptor (APLNR) agonists that preferentially activate protective G protein signaling while avoiding β-arrestin pathways linked to pathological cardiac remodeling. Such G protein-biased agonists represent a promising strategy for treating heart failure, myocardial infarction, and pulmonary arterial hypertension.

papers.title: Thermophysically Guided Design of Spray-Dried Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Microcapsules with Improved Thermal Stability.
papers.abstract: Spray drying and gastrointestinal transit can cause substantial losses in probiotic viability, limiting effective delivery in food applications. This study developed a thermophysically guided framework for the rational design of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum microcapsules in three sequential stages. First, Kissinger kinetic analysis of eleven biopolymer candidates (Ea: 95.4-198.4 kJ/mol) combined with pH-dependent solubility profiling provided an empirical screening criterion for the preselection of coating materials; the activation energies are apparent values associated with a composite endo
papers.summary: This study presents a three-stage framework for designing spray-dried Lactiplantibacillus plantarum microcapsules with improved thermal stability. Using Kissinger kinetic analysis of eleven biopolymer candidates (activation energies 95.4–198.4 kJ/mol) combined with pH-dependent solubility profiling, the authors established an empirical screening criterion for preselection of coating materials. The approach aims to reduce probiotic viability losses during spray drying and gastrointestinal transit.

papers.title: Adhesives Inspired by Marine Organisms: Multifunctional Design and Application for Complex Wet/Underwater Environments.
papers.abstract: Achieving strong adhesion in humid or underwater environments is a long-term challenge in materials science. Water molecules form a hydration layer on the substrate surface, blocking effective contact between the adhesive and the interface, leading to the failure of traditional adhesives. The wet adhesion strength of viscoelastic materials is due to the synergistic effect of interfacial chemical bonds and multiscale energy dissipation, but water environment can seriously interfere with this mechanism. In nature, mussels, barnacles, and sandcastle worms have evolved unique wet adhesion strategi
papers.summary: This review surveys how marine organisms such as mussels, barnacles, and sandcastle worms achieve strong wet adhesion despite the hydration layer that defeats conventional adhesives, and how these biological strategies are being translated into synthetic adhesives. It emphasizes the synergy between interfacial chemical bonding and multiscale energy dissipation as the key design principle for wet/underwater adhesion. The paper is a materials-science review with limited direct bioinformatics content.

papers.title: Microbial Rhodopsins: Structural-Functional Mechanisms and the Design of Optogenetic Silencing Tools-With Emphasis on Halorubrum Archaeorhodopsins.
papers.abstract: Microbial rhodopsins are light-sensitive membrane proteins that use retinal as a covalent chromophore and adopt a seven-transmembrane α-helical fold. They are widely distributed across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi and mediate diverse functions, including light-driven ion transport, light-gated ion conduction, and photosensory signaling. Since the discovery of bacteriorhodopsin in 1971, the microbial rhodopsin family has expanded continuously, and channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics has revolutionized neuroscience by enabling millisecond-scale optical control of neuronal activity. Howeve
papers.summary: This review examines the structural and functional mechanisms of microbial rhodopsins, a family of seven-transmembrane retinal-binding membrane proteins found across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi that perform light-driven ion transport, light-gated ion conduction, and photosensory signaling. It traces the field from the 1971 discovery of bacteriorhodopsin through channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics, with particular attention to Halorubrum archaeorhodopsins and their potential as optogenetic silencing tools. The emphasis on inhibitory/silencing applications addresses a key gap, since most optogenetic work has focused on activation.

papers.title: Rational Design of Molecularly Imprinted Nanozymes for Selective Degradation of Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC).
papers.abstract: Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC) is an engineering thermoplastic whose recycling is hindered by its Code-7 classification and environmental BPA leaching. Here, we report water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes for the selective depolymerization of BPA-PC under mild alkaline conditions. Synthesized within cross-linked surfactant micelles, the optimized nanozyme combines shape-complementary BPA-matched pockets with surface basicity, achieving a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase. Fluorescence titrations with a soluble dansyl-labeled BPA-PC dimer confirm strong subs
papers.summary: The authors designed water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes that selectively depolymerize poly(bisphenol A carbonate) under mild alkaline conditions. The optimized nanozyme combines BPA-shaped binding pockets with surface basicity, achieving a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase. This offers a potential route for recycling a hard-to-recycle plastic and reducing BPA leaching.

papers.title: A Dipeptide Module Substitution-Based Strategy for the Modification and Evaluation of ACE Inhibitory Peptides.
papers.abstract: Food-derived angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitory peptide LYPVK exhibits promising potential for application as an important ingredient with a potential antihypertensive effect in functional foods. However, the structure-activity relationship and the rational design strategy for peptide modification remain insufficiently understood. To address this, dipeptide module substitution was employed to modify and investigate the mechanism of this food-derived ACE inhibitory peptide, providing an insight into the structure-activity relationship. Through integration of molecular docking and ac
papers.summary: This study introduces a dipeptide module substitution strategy to modify the food-derived ACE inhibitory peptide LYPVK, aiming to clarify its structure-activity relationship. By combining molecular docking with activity assays, the authors identify key dipeptide modules that influence ACE inhibition, providing a rational design approach for improving antihypertensive peptides in functional foods.

papers.title: Food-Derived Umami Peptides: Linking Candidate Discovery, Experimental Validation, and Food Applications.
papers.abstract: Alternative proteins and cultivated meat increase the need for flavour strategies that maintain savoury quality with less reliance on salt and conventional seasonings. Food-derived umami peptides are promising candidates, but their practical value depends on evidence beyond sequence prediction. With advances in virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted approaches, discovery is expanding from sensory-guided preparation toward candidate-library construction and data-driven prioritization. This review compares food-protein resources and experimental and sequence-based discovery routes, and
papers.summary: This review examines food-derived umami peptides as a route to savoury flavour with reduced salt and conventional seasoning reliance, especially relevant as alternative proteins and cultivated meat expand. It compares food-protein resources and discovery routes, contrasting sensory-guided preparation with virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted candidate-library prioritisation, and stresses that practical value requires experimental validation beyond sequence prediction.

papers.title: Stoichiometry-dependent gating and structural pharmacology of cardiac GIRK1/4 channels.
papers.abstract: Cardiac G protein-gated inwardly rectifying potassium-K + (GIRK) channels, formed by GIRK1/4 heterotetramers or GIRK4 homotetramers, are crucial regulators of heart rate, and their dysfunction is associated with atrial fibrillation. Despite their therapeutic potential as anti-arrhythmic targets, development of selective GIRK modulators has been limited by an incomplete understanding of their structures, gating mechanisms, and pharmacology. Here, we report high-resolution structures of the GIRK4 homotetramer and of GIRK1/4 heterotetramers, revealing that they form in unexpected 1:3 and 2:2 asse
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study presents high-resolution cryo-EM structures of cardiac GIRK channels, revealing that GIRK1/4 heterotetramers assemble in unexpected 1:3 and 2:2 stoichiometries rather than the assumed 2:2 arrangement. The structures show that subunit stoichiometry influences channel gating and pharmacology, providing a structural basis for developing selective anti-arrhythmic drugs targeting these channels in atrial fibrillation.

papers.title: Whole-proteome structure/function prediction in uropathogenic E. coli reveals previously missed host-microbe and microbe-phage interaction pathways.
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of high-throughput sequencing technologies has vastly increased the number of known protein sequences, but the experimental characterization of their structures and functions lags behind. This gap in knowledge impedes our understanding of biological mechanisms of these proteins, hinders the interpretation of high-throughput experiments, and exposes a significant challenge in modern biology: deducing the structural and functional information of proteins based on their sequences. Most computational approaches rely on homology with well-annotated proteins, yet many proteins
papers.summary: The authors applied whole-proteome structure and function prediction to uropathogenic E. coli, going beyond homology-based annotation to uncover previously uncharacterized proteins. This revealed host-microbe and microbe-phage interaction pathways that had been missed by conventional annotation approaches. The work demonstrates the value of structure-based proteome-wide prediction for filling functional knowledge gaps in bacterial pathogens.

papers.title: Tomatidine derivatives suppress Dengue virus infection through entry and post-entry inhibition.
papers.abstract: Dengue is a rapidly spreading disease transmitted by mosquitoes and is caused by the Dengue virus (DENV), affecting approximately 390 million individuals globally. Approved vaccines for use have limited efficacy, and there are no approved antivirals. Tomatidine, a steroidal alkaloid obtained from Solanum species, has demonstrated broad-spectrum antiviral properties, leading to the investigation of its derivatives for their anti-DENV activity. In the current study, the anti-DENV potential of tomatidine and 11 such derivatives was assessed using a combination of in vitro and in silico approaches
papers.summary: This study tested tomatidine, a steroidal alkaloid from Solanum plants, along with 11 derivatives for activity against Dengue virus using in vitro and computational approaches. Several derivatives suppressed DENV infection by blocking both viral entry and post-entry steps, suggesting these compounds could serve as leads for antiviral development against dengue, for which no approved drugs currently exist.

papers.title: From structure prediction to ligand-target recognition: expanding the reach of AlphaFold in natural product research.
papers.abstract: Natural products constitute a structurally diverse reservoir of bioactive molecules and remain an important source of lead compounds for drug discovery. However, the limited availability of structural information on pharmacological targets and biomolecular interactions continues to hinder mechanism elucidation and structure-guided optimization, particularly for complex natural products such as bioactive peptides, proteinaceous natural products, and natural molecular glues. Recent advances in AlphaFold have transformed structural biology by enabling high-confidence prediction of protein structu
papers.summary: This review discusses how AlphaFold's protein structure prediction capabilities can be extended beyond structure determination to help identify ligand-target interactions relevant to natural product research. It highlights applications for challenging molecules like bioactive peptides and molecular glues, where limited structural data has hindered mechanism elucidation and optimization.

papers.title: Atomistic insights into the migration and diffusion behavior of crosslinking byproducts in polyethylene networks.
papers.abstract: The accumulation of crosslinking byproducts, such as cumyl alcohol and acetophenone, in polyethylene (PE) insulation accelerates the degradation of high-voltage direct current (HVDC) cables through space charge formation and electrical tree propagation. Since conventional degassing processes cannot entirely eliminate these crosslinking byproducts, characterizing their residual dynamic behavior is of paramount importance. This work presents a comprehensive molecular dynamics (MD) simulation study to quantify the diffusion kinetics of these byproducts within the PE network. By systematically var
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to quantify how crosslinking byproducts (cumyl alcohol and acetophenone) migrate and diffuse through polyethylene networks used in high-voltage cable insulation. The work characterizes the diffusion kinetics of these residual molecules, which cannot be fully removed by conventional degassing and contribute to insulation degradation. The findings provide atomistic-level insight into byproduct mobility that could inform improved degassing strategies.

papers.title: Unrevealed oligoresveratrols from Shorea parvifolia root bark as xanthine oxidase inhibitors: isolation, in vitro bioassay, quantum studies and structure-based computational profiling.
papers.abstract: Resveratrol oligomers from Shorea species possess diverse biological activities, but the structural determinants governing their inhibition of xanthine oxidase (XO) remain poorly understood. This study investigated oligoresveratrols isolated from the root bark of Shorea parvifolia and examined how their structures relate to XO inhibitory potential. Five oligoresveratrols were isolated and structurally characterized by spectroscopic analysis. We evaluated their XO inhibitory activities, followed by pharmacokinetic and drug-likeness predictions, DFT calculations, molecular docking, and molecular
papers.summary: This study isolated five resveratrol oligomers from Shorea parvifolia root bark and tested their ability to inhibit xanthine oxidase, an enzyme target relevant to gout and oxidative stress. The authors combined in vitro enzyme assays with quantum chemical calculations, pharmacokinetic predictions, and molecular docking to explore how structural features of these compounds relate to inhibitory activity. The work provides a structure-activity framework for plant-derived oligoresveratrols as potential xanthine oxidase inhibitors.

papers.title: Integrated experimental and computational study of a novel indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane as a potential inhibitor of Mcl-1.
papers.abstract: Myeloid cell leukemia-1 (Mcl-1) is a key anti-apoptotic protein that drives resistance to chemotherapy, making it a critical oncology target. In this study, we synthesized a new indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane via a one-pot multicomponent reaction and characterized its structure by FT-IR, 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, and mass spectrometry. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the B3LYP/6-31G (d) level were carried out to study its electronic features and reactive centers. In molecular docking against Mcl-1, the propellane derivative showed a binding score of -5.678 kcal mol-1, outperfor
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a new indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane compound and characterized it spectroscopically, then used DFT calculations and molecular docking to assess its potential as an inhibitor of the anti-apoptotic cancer target Mcl-1. Docking suggested a modest binding affinity (-5.678 kcal/mol) that outperformed a comparator, but no experimental validation of Mcl-1 inhibition or cellular activity was reported.

papers.title: Structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference in an infant-derived Bifidobacterium bifidum PNGaseA.
papers.abstract: N-glycans are abundant nutrient sources for human gut bacteria, which deploy peptide: N-glycosidases to release them from glycoproteins. Breast milk is comprised of a high proportion of N-glycosylated bioactive proteins that can be accessed by infant colonic microbes. Here, we biochemically and structurally characterize a PNGaseA-family enzyme from infant-associated Bifidobacterium bifidum LMG13195. This enzyme acts on a broad range of N-glycan structures but shows a marked preference for N-glycans attached to glycopeptides rather than to denatured or native proteins, highlighting a specialize
papers.summary: Researchers characterized a PNGaseA-family enzyme from Bifidobacterium bifidum, a bacterium found in infant guts, that cleaves N-glycans from glycoproteins. The enzyme works on a wide range of N-glycan structures but strongly prefers glycopeptides over intact proteins, suggesting it specializes in processing partially digested milk glycoproteins. Structural and biochemical analyses reveal the basis for this substrate preference.

papers.title: Full-fat soybean origin and thermal processing affect protein secondary structure, in vitro digestion kinetics, and predicted standardized ileal amino acid digestibility in broiler chickens.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the chemical composition, protein secondary structure, crude protein (CP) solubilization, and in-vitro amino acid (AA) digestibility of three Kenyan full-fat soybean (FFSB) samples (S1, S2, S3) with unknown processing histories and compared with Canadian samples: raw FFSB, extruded FFSB at 160.0 °C, and FFSB roasted at 136.7 °C, 151.7 °C, or 154.4 °C. Protein structure was characterized using attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. A two-phase in-vitro digestion model was used to determine CP solubilization and AA digestibility. Observed in-vi
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This study shows that the origin and thermal processing history of full-fat soybeans (Kenyan vs. Canadian samples, raw vs. extruded vs. roasted at various temperatures) significantly alter protein secondary structure, as measured by FTIR spectroscopy. These structural differences translate into different in vitro digestion kinetics and predicted standardized ileal amino acid digestibility for broiler chickens. The work highlights that processing conditions and sourcing must be accounted for when evaluating soybean meal quality as poultry feed.

papers.title: Exploration of vetiver-derived compounds for addressing remedy against male infertility using in silco approach.
papers.abstract: The rising prevalence of reproductive disorders, including male infertility, necessitates innovative therapeutic strategies. Plant-based extracts, particularly those from Chrysopogon zizanioides (vetiver plant), have emerged as promising candidates. This study employs in silico methodologies to evaluate the therapeutic potential of vetiver-derived compounds against male infertility. This research aims to investigate the pharmacokinetic profiles, bioactivity, toxicity, and molecular interactions of vetiver compounds with proteins implicated in male reproductive health.
papers.summary: This study uses computational (in silico) methods to screen compounds derived from the vetiver plant (Chrysopogon zizanioides) for potential activity against proteins implicated in male infertility. The authors assess pharmacokinetic properties, bioactivity, toxicity, and molecular docking interactions, aiming to identify plant-based candidates for treating reproductive disorders. The work is exploratory and relies entirely on computational prediction without experimental validation.

papers.title: Phytochemical Screening, Pharmacological Evaluation, and Exploratory In Silico Analysis of Emilia sonchifolia Extract and Solvent Fractions.
papers.abstract: Emilia sonchifolia (L.) DC. is a medicinal plant used traditionally for the management of several disorders; however, integrated experimental evaluation of its pharmacological properties remains limited. This study evaluated the phytochemical composition and selected biological activities of the methanolic whole-plant extract of E. sonchifolia (MEES) and its solvent-partitioned fractions and explored possible molecular interactions of literature-reported pyrrolizidine alkaloids using computational approaches. Qualitative phytochemical screening, brine shrimp lethality, 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhyd
papers.summary: This study screened the methanolic extract and solvent fractions of the medicinal plant Emilia sonchifolia for phytochemical content and biological activities, including brine shrimp lethality and antioxidant assays. It also used computational docking to explore possible molecular interactions of literature-reported pyrrolizidine alkaloids. The work is largely descriptive and preliminary, combining standard phytochemical screening with in silico exploration.

papers.title: A Scalable, Traceable Computational-to-Experimental Pipeline for Activity-Guided Identification of Bioactive Constituents: A Case Study in Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge.
papers.abstract: Systematic identification of bioactive constituents from complex natural products remains challenging. Here, a scalable and traceable integrated workflow was developed and validated in Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge (SMB) for anti-Parkinson's disease (PD) constituent discovery. Network pharmacology first identified four candidate compounds, which were quantified and dynamically tracked during X-5 macroporous resin enrichment and fractionation using a validated HPLC method. Transfer rates exceeded 80% for all candidates, confirming efficient enrichment and chemical traceability. Bioactivity was then
papers.summary: The authors developed an integrated computational-to-experimental pipeline for discovering bioactive compounds in the medicinal plant Salvia miltiorrhiza, targeting Parkinson's disease. Network pharmacology prioritized four candidate compounds, which were then tracked through enrichment and fractionation steps using validated HPLC, with transfer rates above 80% confirming chemical traceability. This provides a scalable, traceable workflow for activity-guided natural product discovery.

papers.title: Development of Novel Furan-Chalcone Derivatives as Targeting Bacterial DNA Gyrase and Topoisomerase IV: Design, Synthesis, and In Silico Studies.
papers.abstract: A series of novel furan-chalcone derivatives (Na1-Na8) were synthesized and evaluated for their antimicrobial, antioxidant, DNA gyrase inhibitory, and computational properties using integrated in vitro and in silico approaches. Among the synthesized compounds, Na5 exhibited the most potent antibacterial activity with low MIC values against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial strains. Antioxidant studies revealed significant free radical scavenging activity for Na3, Na4, and Na5. Molecular docking studies against DNA gyrase B demonstrated favorable binding interactions within the ATP
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis and evaluation of eight novel furan-chalcone derivatives, with compound Na5 showing the strongest antibacterial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Several compounds also showed notable antioxidant activity, and molecular docking suggested they bind to the ATP site of bacterial DNA gyrase B, a known antibiotic target. The work is preliminary, relying on in vitro assays and computational predictions without in vivo validation.

papers.title: Shexiang Huayu Xingnao Granule Alleviates Intracerebral Hemorrhage via PI3K/AKT-Mediated Neuroinflammation Regulation: Integrated Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Employing network pharmacology prediction combined with experimental validation, this research elucidated the underlying mechanisms of Shexiang Huayu Xingnao granules (SXHY) against intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH).
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology predictions followed by experimental validation to show that Shexiang Huayu Xingnao granules reduce neuroinflammation after intracerebral hemorrhage through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. The work combines computational target prediction with in vivo/in vitro experiments to support a mechanistic explanation for a traditional Chinese medicine formulation.

papers.title: A split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers define the tail architecture of Pseudomonas aeruginosa podophage A1002.
papers.abstract: Phage therapy offers unique advantages against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. However, high-resolution structural studies of phages targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa-a top-seven global pathogen-particularly podophages, remain severely limited, directly impeding structure-based development of novel antimicrobials. In this study, we utilize cryo-EM to resolve the high-resolution intact structure of mature phage A1002, a podophage infecting carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa. Based on density maps combined with AlphaFold3 predictions, we identified 11 structural protein components from the head to
papers.summary: This study uses cryo-EM to determine the high-resolution structure of podophage A1002, which infects carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The authors identify 11 structural proteins and describe a novel split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fiber architecture in the phage tail. These structural insights could aid structure-based design of phage-based antimicrobials.

papers.title: Fragment-based active-site exploration of urethane hydrolases reveals a diversity of urethane binding modes.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in the discovery, characterization and engineering of urethanases provide new opportunities for the sustainable biocatalytic degradation of polyurethane waste. A mechanistic understanding of enzyme-plastic interactions is essential for structure-based engineering to enhance urethanase activity. However, the extremely complex and hydrophobic nature of polyurethane makes it challenging to elucidate the structural basis of enzyme-plastic interactions. Here, we used a fragment-based approach to characterize the active sites of two novel urethanases called amidase U11 and esterase A
papers.journal: Acta crystallographica. Section D, Structural biology
papers.summary: This study uses a fragment-based crystallographic approach to probe the active sites of two newly identified urethane hydrolases, amidase U11 and esterase A. The work reveals that urethane binds in multiple distinct orientations within these enzymes, highlighting the structural diversity of enzyme-plastic interactions. These findings provide a foundation for structure-based engineering to improve the biocatalytic degradation of polyurethane waste.

papers.title: Aptamers without SELEX: De novo design from protein structure in hours.
papers.abstract: Systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX)-based aptamer discovery can be constrained by target availability, selection biases, and optimization requirements. We introduce Xelari, a modular pipeline for de novo DNA and RNA aptamer design from protein structures without target-specific SELEX data or retraining. Xelari combines algorithmic modules with surrogate models trained on physical or structural references. InNA reproduced nucleotide-amino-acid interaction energies with RMSE of 0.19 kcal/mol across 483,735 reference pairs. AliNA achieved a mean F1 of 0.757 on 339 PD
papers.summary: Xelari is a modular computational pipeline that designs DNA and RNA aptamers directly from protein structures without requiring SELEX selection data or target-specific model retraining. Its surrogate models reproduce nucleotide-amino-acid interaction energies and predict binding interfaces with strong accuracy, enabling aptamer design in hours rather than weeks. This could substantially accelerate aptamer discovery by removing the target-availability and selection-bias bottlenecks of SELEX.

papers.title: The Plant-Derived Peptide Hyde C1 Exhibits Membrane-Associated Antifungal Activity and Protects Against Systemic Candida albicans Infection.
papers.abstract: Invasive candidiasis and increasing antifungal resistance underscore the need for alternative therapeutic approaches. Antimicrobial peptides are of interest because of their antifungal activity and potential membrane-associated effects. This study evaluated Hyde C1, a plant-derived antimicrobial peptide from Cichorium intybus, for antifungal activity against Candida albicans and examined whether its effects were associated with fungal membrane-associated effects.
papers.summary: The plant-derived peptide Hyde C1, from chicory, shows antifungal activity against Candida albicans that appears linked to effects on the fungal membrane, and it protected mice against systemic infection. This suggests Hyde C1 could be a starting point for new antifungal therapies amid rising resistance.

papers.title: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and cancer: knowledge mapping and emerging trends based on a bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: To systematically map the global publication landscape, collaboration patterns, thematic structure, and emerging research activity in the literature on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and cancer.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the global research landscape on PFAS and cancer, identifying publication trends, collaboration networks, and emerging thematic areas. It provides a structured overview of the field's growth and highlights key research clusters and gaps. The study is descriptive and does not present new experimental findings.

papers.title: Quercetin attenuates acute inflammation and extracellular matrix remodeling after intracerebral hemorrhage: transcriptomics-informed network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) induces secondary brain injury characterized by neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, oxidative stress, and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Quercetin (QR), a natural flavonoid with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has shown neuroprotective potential; however, the molecular signatures associated with its effects in acute ICH remain incompletely defined. In this study, QR-related target prediction, ICH-associated gene mining, endoplasmic reticulum stress-related gene annotation, and 2 mouse brain transcriptomic datasets were integra
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology, transcriptomic datasets, and experimental validation to show that quercetin reduces acute neuroinflammation and extracellular matrix remodeling after intracerebral hemorrhage in mice. The authors identify molecular targets and pathways linking quercetin's anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects to improved outcomes in the acute phase of ICH.

papers.title: Integrative network toxicology and machine learning reveal the potential role of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural in exacerbating pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF), a ubiquitous furan derivative formed during the thermal processing of carbohydrate-rich foods, represents a widespread dietary exposure. However, its potential contribution to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains unclear. This study investigated the molecular links between 5-HMF and IPF using an integrated computational and experimental approach.
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology and machine learning to identify molecular pathways linking dietary 5-HMF exposure to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, supported by experimental validation. It suggests 5-HMF may exacerbate IPF through specific target genes and pathways, though the evidence is largely computational.

papers.title: Comparative Hydrophobicity Analysis of Human β-Tubulin and Bacterial FtsZ Using the Fuzzy Oil Drop Model: Potential Implications for Chaperone-Assisted Folding.
papers.abstract: The issue of protein folding in vivo remains an unsolved problem despite important progress achieved by artificial intelligence (AlphaFold). Experimental studies have shown that there are several mechanisms involved in this process. The main distinction concerns the involvement of chaperone proteins in this process as opposed to spontaneous folding. Evolutionary analysis shows that tubulin in eukaryotic organisms requires engagement of the ATP-dependent ring-shaped chaperonin TRiC/CCT, while the homologous protein in prokaryotic organisms obtains its functional structure without the support fr
papers.summary: This computational study compares the hydrophobicity patterns of human β-tubulin and its bacterial homolog FtsZ using the Fuzzy Oil Drop model, which describes how proteins bury hydrophobic residues in their cores. The authors find that tubulin's hydrophobic distribution is less ideal (more exposed hydrophobic patches) than FtsZ's, which they suggest may explain why eukaryotic tubulin requires chaperonin-assisted folding while bacterial FtsZ can fold spontaneously. The work offers a structural rationale linking hydrophobicity profiles to chaperone dependence across evolution.

papers.title: HNRNPH2-R114W remodels RNA splicing and neurodevelopmental gene programs in isogenic cerebral organoids.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder has been linked to disrupted RNA processing during corticogenesis, yet variant-specific mechanisms remain difficult to resolve. Isogenic cerebral organoids derived from a patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) line carrying the HNRNPH2-R114W variant and its CRISPR-corrected counterpart serve as a human developmental model to investigate variant-associated RNA dysregulation. Imaging quantification and exploratory bulk RNA sequencing, performed at a single developmental time point on a pooled organoid RNA from each genotype, identify coordinated remodeling
papers.summary: Using isogenic cerebral organoids derived from a patient iPSC line carrying the HNRNPH2-R114W autism-associated variant and its CRISPR-corrected counterpart, the authors show that the variant remodels RNA splicing and alters neurodevelopmental gene expression programs. Imaging and bulk RNA-seq at a single developmental time point reveal coordinated transcriptomic changes linked to the mutation. This provides a human developmental model for variant-specific RNA dysregulation in corticogenesis.

papers.title: Integrated in vitro and in silico assessment of antimicrobial, chemical antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities of endophytic Aspergillus sp. GK1 isolated from Mentha spicata roots.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants are a source of structurally diverse endophytic fungi which harbor significant pharmaceutical potential.
papers.summary: This study isolated the endophytic fungus Aspergillus sp. GK1 from Mentha spicata roots and characterized its antimicrobial, antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities using both in vitro assays and in silico molecular docking. The fungus produced bioactive compounds with promising antimicrobial and antioxidant effects and showed cytotoxicity against certain cell lines, suggesting its potential as a source of pharmaceutical leads. The work highlights endophytic fungi from medicinal plants as a valuable reservoir for drug discovery.

papers.title: InRegPep: a web server for modeling of parallel beta-sheet fibrillar aggregates of amyloidogenic peptides.
papers.abstract: Predicting the structures of peptide or protein aggregates that assemble into amyloid protofilaments remains one of the most challenging tasks in computational structural biology. Computational difficulties arise mainly from the large size of the modeled systems and the extensive timescales of aggregation processes. The InRegPep web server is designed for the multiscale structural modeling of peptide aggregates that preferentially adopt in-register parallel β-sheet architectures. The method employs the coarse-grained CABS model, which enables the assembly of a large number of aggregates compos
papers.summary: InRegPep is a web server that predicts the 3D structures of amyloid-like peptide aggregates that form in-register parallel beta-sheet fibrils. It uses a coarse-grained CABS model to assemble many peptides into aggregate structures, addressing the size and timescale challenges that make such modeling difficult. The tool is aimed at researchers studying amyloidogenic peptides and their fibrillar assemblies.

papers.title: Structure-based minimization of a high-mobility group protein B1 (HMGB1) B box peptide uncouples anti-NETotic activity and anti-biofilm function.
papers.abstract: We previously showed that human HMGB1 has anti-biofilm activity localized to a 97-amino-acid B-Box-derived peptide (mB Box-97), engineered with a C106S mutation to reduce HMGB1's proinflammatory properties while retaining anti-biofilm function. This peptide also suppresses NETosis by inhibiting neutrophil protein kinase C (PKC) activity. Here, we tested whether the anti-biofilm and anti-NETotic activities of mB Box-97 could be separated into distinct shorter peptides by constructing truncated variants containing Helix 1 of the B-Box (with the C106S mutation), with or without the A Box-B Box li
papers.summary: The authors previously engineered a 97-amino-acid HMGB1 B-box peptide (mB Box-97) that retains anti-biofilm activity while suppressing NETosis via PKC inhibition. Here they tested truncated variants containing Helix 1 of the B-box to determine whether the anti-biofilm and anti-NETotic activities could be separated into distinct shorter peptides, finding that these functions can be uncoupled.

papers.title: Unleashing the industrial potential of microbial plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes: recent advances in protein engineering.
papers.abstract: Plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes (PCWPEs) used in industry are predominantly of microbial origin. Key enzyme classes, including cellulases, lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases (LPMOs), β-xylanases, β-mannanases and pectinases, have attained technological maturity and are widely deployed across agro-waste biorefineries, food and feed processing, textile and pulp manufacturing. Low catalytic efficiency, insufficient thermostability, poor operational adaptability, restricted functionality, and product inhibition limit the industrial use of these enzymes. Structure- and sequence-gu
papers.summary: This review surveys recent protein engineering advances aimed at improving microbial plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes (cellulases, LPMOs, xylanases, mannanases, pectinases) for industrial use. It focuses on overcoming limitations such as low catalytic efficiency, poor thermostability, and product inhibition through structure- and sequence-guided engineering strategies. The paper consolidates progress toward making these enzymes more robust and adaptable for biorefineries, food/feed processing, textiles, and pulp manufacturing.
